classes.name: GLP-1-based anti-obesity medications
classes.description: Injectable or oral GLP-1/GIP agents labeled for chronic weight management (NOT their diabetes-labeled versions): semaglutide (Wegovy, including Wegovy tablets), tirzepatide (Zepbound), liraglutide (Saxenda). Many plans exclude weight-loss drugs entirely; an exclusion is a valid finding (outcome nonformulary).
classes.plainDescription: A weekly shot (or daily pill) for weight loss, like Wegovy or Zepbound.

classes.name: Oral anti-obesity medications
classes.description: Oral anti-obesity agents: phentermine (Adipex-P, Lomaira), phentermine/topiramate ER (Qsymia), naltrexone/bupropion ER (Contrave), orlistat (Xenical). Many plans exclude weight-loss drugs; an exclusion is a valid finding (outcome nonformulary).
classes.plainDescription: A pill for weight loss, like phentermine or Contrave.

records.preferredRestriction: No weight-loss GLP-1 (Wegovy, Zepbound, Saxenda) appears on this PDL (searched, none listed). The PDL does not state it is a complete coverage list; it directs readers to the Texas Medicaid Formulary search to verify coverage. Coverage unconfirmed; confirm there.
records.verificationNote: Searched the full PDL (88 pp.) for Wegovy, Zepbound, Saxenda, liraglutide, tirzepatide, semaglutide, and weight/obesity terms. No weight-management GLP-1 is listed. The diabetes-labeled GLP-1s (OZEMPIC, RYBELSUS, VICTOZA, MOUNJARO, TRULICITY, p.49) do not count for this class. No exclusion is inferred: the PDL page footer only says to verify coverage in the Medicaid Formulary search, and does not state whether the list is complete. Coverage is unconfirmed. [Sonnet check 2026-10-21: removed the unsupported claim that the PDL footer says the list is not complete; the footer (e.g. p.27, p.80) only points to the Formulary search.]

records.verificationNote: Weight-loss GLP-1s are not on this plan's list. Wegovy, Zepbound and Saxenda do not appear anywhere in the document (full text searched). Mounjaro (page 43) and Ozempic (page 44) are listed under the Blood Glucose Regulators category (page 42) with PA and QL; the document does not give them a weight-management indication, so they are not treated as covered weight-loss options. The document contains no statement that it is a complete list, so absence is recorded as a finding to confirm, not a stated exclusion.

records.verificationNote: No phentermine, phentermine/topiramate (Qsymia), naltrexone/bupropion ER (Contrave) or orlistat (Xenical) line appears in the document (full text searched). Lines that look similar but are not weight-loss agents: naltrexone 50 mg tablet (anti-addiction, Tier 2, page 13), bupropion SR/ER (smoking deterrent, Tier 3, pages 13 and 21-22), topiramate tablet and solution (anticonvulsant, page 20). The document contains no statement that it is a complete list, so absence is recorded as a finding to confirm, not a stated exclusion.
